描述_EN: in 2016, cnn reported that the average american spends 10 hours+ looking at screens (including, but not limited to the smartphone), and that the average person looks at around 5000+ ads a day (both digital and analogue). irl glasses were sent to backers (supporters of a campaign) in april 2019. at the time of the irl glasses' creation, the irl lab core staff were founder ivan cash, scott blew (head of product & inventor), emily lin, dominic gallelli and james simonetta. the irl ‘screen blocking’ sunglasses were designed by irl labs in san francisco, california (us) in 2018. the irl (‘in real life’) glasses were created by irl labs as a response to the proliferation of digital screens that we come into contact with in everyday life, from tvs in bars to advertising billboards. irl labs have presented the irl glasses to serve as a provocation and critique, and as a proof-of-concept for the future development of glasses that are able to block all digital media. irl glasses were invented by scott blew (irl head of product) and brought to market by irl labs, led by founder ivan cash. the irl glasses are made from solid black plastic with plastic lenses. the irl glasses join the snap spectacles and google glass as examples of technological eyewear, and underlines the impact that digital culture and media has had on eyewear design. the lenses are standard tac 1.1, cat 3, uv 400; with the uv block also function independently as sunglasses. the packaging, designed by brad kayal and manufactured by gpa global (california, us), is a 3-piece box including an internal glasses mount with silver printing, a lenticular box with four animated frames of tv static, and a clear acrylic slipcase with white printing. from their company mission statement, irl labs is ‘a creative incubator empowering humanity to free itself from the unhealthy constraints of technology’. the glasses use a horizontal polarized optics filter that blocks out led and lcd screens, rendering their content unreadable, the screens and content going ‘blank’ as they are viewed. the glasses were manufactured in wenzhou, china, with manufacturer so-pal optics. the outside of the box was designed to be a representation of a chaotic digital environment, with a simple black interior to emphasise the effect of the glasses. however, the glasses do not block 4k video, oled (organic light-emitting diode) or smartphone screens. using kickstarter as their only source of funding, the campaign to raise funds for the glasses was announced on october 1st 2018. their target was successfully reached by october 31st 2018, with $140,920 pledged by 2,030 backers. they were designed to closely replicate the design of the glasses in john carpenter’s 198 film ‘they live’, which serves as the main inspiration for the glasses themselves. by flattening and rotating the polarized lens 90 degrees, light emitted by lcd/led screens is blocked. projects include ‘no tech zone’ in san francisco which designates technology-free areas to provoke non-digital communication, and snail mail my email, which sends emails physically by post. ivan cash is also founder of cash studios, where his looks at the relationship that society has with technology. this simple, lightweight, design allows wearers to choose and limit their exposure to most digital content.
描述_ZN: 2016年，Cnn报道说，美国人平均花10个小时以上的时间看屏幕（包括但不限于智能手机），平均每人每天看大约5000多个广告（包括数字和模拟）。 2019年4月，女孩眼镜被送到支持者（活动的支持者）手中。 at the time of the irl glasses' creation, the irl lab core staff were founder ivan cash, scott blew (head of product & inventor), emily lin, dominic gallelli and james simonetta. irl "阻挡屏幕 "太阳镜是由位于美国加州圣弗朗西斯科的irl实验室于2018年设计的。 irl（"在现实生活中"）眼镜是由irl labs创造的，作为对我们在日常生活中接触到的从酒吧的电视到广告牌的数字屏幕扩散的回应。 irl实验室推出的irl眼镜是一种挑衅和批判，也是对未来能够屏蔽所有数字媒体的眼镜发展的一个概念验证。 irl眼镜由Scott blew（irl产品负责人）发明，并由创始人Ivan cash领导的irl实验室推向市场。 irl眼镜由纯黑色塑料制成，带有塑料镜片。 irl眼镜与snap眼镜和google glass一样是科技眼镜的典范，并强调了数字文化和媒体对眼镜设计的影响。 the lenses are standard tac 1.1, cat 3, uv 400; with the uv block also function independently as sunglasses. 包装由Brad Kayal设计，由GPA Global（美国加州）制造，是一个3件套的盒子，包括一个银色印刷的内部眼镜支架，一个带有四个电视静态动画帧的光栅盒，以及一个白色印刷的透明丙烯酸滑套。 从他们的公司使命声明来看，irl labs是 "一个创造性的孵化器，使人类能够从技术的不健康约束中解放出来"。 该眼镜使用一种水平偏振光学过滤器，可以阻挡LED和LCD屏幕，使其内容无法阅读，屏幕和内容在观看时是 "空白 "的。 该眼镜在中国温州制造，由制造商So-pal optics生产。 盒子的外部被设计成一个混乱的数字环境的代表，简单的黑色内部强调了眼镜的效果。 然而，该眼镜不能阻挡4K视频、OLED（有机发光二极管）或智能手机屏幕。 使用kickstarter作为他们唯一的资金来源，为该眼镜筹集资金的活动于2018年10月1日宣布。 他们的目标在2018年10月31日之前成功达成，由2030名支持者认捐了140,920美元。 它们被设计成密切复制约翰-卡彭特198年的电影《他们的生活》中的眼镜设计，这也是眼镜本身的主要灵感来源。 通过将偏光镜片拉平并旋转90度，可以阻挡LCD/LED屏幕发出的光线。 项目包括在旧金山的 "无技术区"，它指定了无技术的区域，以激起非数字的交流，以及蜗牛邮件我的邮件，它通过邮寄的方式发送电子邮件。 伊万-卡什也是卡什工作室的创始人，他在那里关注社会与技术的关系。 这种简单、轻便的设计使佩戴者可以选择并限制他们对大多数数字内容的接触。
